'''Friederich Pius Philipp Furtwängler''' (April 21, 1869 – May 19, 1940) was a German [[number theorist]].

==Biography==
Furtwängler wrote an 1896 doctoral dissertation at the [[University of Göttingen]] on [[cubic form]]s (''Zur Theorie der in Linearfaktoren zerlegbaren ganzzahligen ternären kubischen Formen''), under [[Felix Klein]]. Most of his academic life, from 1912 to 1938, was spent at the [[University of Vienna]], where he taught for example [[Kurt Gödel]], who later said that Furtwängler's lectures on number theory were the best mathematical lectures that he ever heard; Gödel had originally intended to become a physicist but turned to mathematics partly as a result of Furtwängler's lectures. From 1916, Furtwängler became increasingly paralysed<ref>{{cite web | url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Furtwangler | title=Philipp Furtwängler - Biography }}</ref> and, without notes, lectured from a wheelchair while his assistant wrote equations on the blackboard.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Moore, Gregory|title=The Incomplete Gödel|journal=American Scientist|date=Sep–Oct 2005|volume=93|issue=5|page=464|doi=10.1511/2005.55.464|url=https://www.americanscientist.org/bookshelf/pub/the-incomplete-g-del|url-access=subscription|archive-date=2017-03-25|access-date=2012-09-17|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170325211022/http://www.americanscientist.org/bookshelf/pub/the-incomplete-g-del|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Some of Furtwängler's doctoral students were [[Wolfgang Gröbner]], [[Nikolaus Hofreiter]], [[Henry Mann]], [[Otto Schreier]], and [[Olga Taussky-Todd]]. Through these and others, he has over 3000 [[academic genealogy|academic descendants]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy |id=7443}}</ref>

He is now best known for his contribution to the [[principal ideal theorem]] in the form of his ''Beweis des Hauptidealsatzes für Klassenkörper algebraischer Zahlkörper'' (1929).

Philipp Furtwängler was a grandson of the organ builder [[:de:Philipp Furtwängler & Söhne|Philipp Furtwängler]] (1800-1867) and a second cousin of the conductor [[Wilhelm Furtwängler]].<ref>[[:de:Furtwängler (Familie)|Furtwängler family tree]]</ref>
